text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN SALE - A major Thai feed producer may have been in the market for 15,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for October shipment, trade sources said. The price was said to be around $335 per tonne C&F Bangkok. The purchase might have been made as part of a government low-tariff programme. Thailand allowed 426,460 tonnes to be imported under the program in 1996.
SOYBEAN MEAL - The CCC bought 3,000 tonnes soybean meal for donation to Georgia. The meal was acquired at $316.83 a tonne, FOB, from Continental Grain for Oct 10-Nov 5 shipment.

CORN SALE - South Africa's Western Cape Maize Buyers Association awarded yellow maize tenders totalling 190,000 tonnes to a number of players for delivery from September until April 1997. A 35,000 tonne tender had been awarded to Cargill at 768.88 rand a tonne for November delivery.
- The South African Maize Board said there was no sale for the export of 33,000 tonnes of white maize for shipment in October and November.
CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwanese buyers are expected to hold four tenders for a total of 104,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 88,000 tonnes of corn next week, traders said.
CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - cont'd - State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp was seen tendering for a combined shipment of 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans, they said.
Taiwan Sugar's shipment is scheduled for delivery from the U.S. Gulf from October 25 to November 10.
WHEAT AND BARLEY TENDER - The Food Agency of Japan said on Thursday it did not carry out its import tender for wheat and barley this week.

WHEAT TENDER - Surinam will be seeking to purchase 2,800 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better northern spring/dark northern spring wheat in bulk under the PL 480 Title I. Shipment is set for October 10-25. Bids must be submitted by September 26.

- Pakistan will tender for 200,000 tonnes U.S.grade 2 or better soft white wheat under the GSM-102 program for October 10-31 shipment, its U.S. export agent said. Bids are due September 29 and must remain valid until September 30.
- The CCC seeks up to 35,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 or better hrw or srw or soft white wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment is set for Oct 10-Nov 5. Offers are due by Sept 26.

WHEAT TENDERS cont'd - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 is the final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.

RICE TENDER - Sri Lanka will decide on awarding a 50,000 tonne rice tender on Friday, the state buying arm Cooperative Wholesale Establishment (CWE) said. Forty one exporters have responded to a Sri Lankan government tender for 50,000 tonnes of rice for October/November delivery.
- Moldova will tender Wednesday for 14,000 tonnes of PL-480 long-grain milled rice for November.

MARKET TALK - Russia may import European and U.S. grain due to its own poor harvest and low output in neighbouring countries, grain sources said. A source at a Western commodities house said he thought Russia's Far East could buy up to 500,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for delivery in November or December. "No deals have been struck, but they will probably go through Roskhleboprodukt (the semi-state buying agency)," the source said. "The Far East's got the money, and don't ask me from where because I don't know."
... Malaysia and Indonesia are looking to buy up to 100,000 tonnes of soymeal for late-1996 delivery, but are holding back because they find prices too high, regional traders said on Thursday.
